title: Abort GPU communicators concurrently to avoid getting stuck.
body:
Abort GPU communicators concurrently to avoid getting stuck.

Recall that when a GPU PjRt client detects that a process has failed, it will
attempt to abort all communicators with that process as a participant.
Previously, the communicators were aborted serially, but this was leading to a
deadlock.

Consider a deployment with three processes: A, B, and C. There are two
communicators: one for A, B, and C and one for A and C. Imagine C fails during
a collective on the ABC communicator. If process A attempts to abort the AC
communicator before the ABC communicator, the cancellation of the AC
communicator gets blocked by the pending collective, and the collective is
never cancelled because the ABC communicator is not aborted until after the AC
communicator.

This commit changes the aborts to happen concurrently and was suggested by the
NCCL team. Emprically, it has solved the problem so far.

title: Allow NCCL communicator creation to be canceled.
body:
Allow NCCL communicator creation to be canceled.

Recall that to perform NCCL collectives (e.g., AllReduce, AllGather), a process
creates a NCCL communicator and then uses the communicator to perform
collectives. If a participant of a collective fails, the collective can hang
forever. However, we can abort a NCCL communicator which aborts all pending
collectives being performed on it.

Creating a communicator can also block if a participant fails, but the code
didn't support canceling the creation of the communicator. This change allows
for communicator creation to be aborted.

The change isn't very deep. It's mostly just plumbing around some
`atomic_bool`s which are set to true when we want to cancel.

title: Hlo module splitting
body:
Hlo module splitting

This change introduces the ability to split a single HLO module into multiple modules, for the separate compilation effort.

Splitting strategy assigns each computation in the call graph (starting from the entry computation) to its own separate module. Calls between computations that end up in different modules are replaced by stubs, which are implemented as custom-calls. An HloLinkingManifest is generated alongside the split modules, containing information to link the modules back together by replacing stubs with calls to the actual computations in other modules.

This change also adds helper methods to assign deterministic instruction and computation IDs, which are used to generate stable module names, and to replace called computations when inserting stubs.

title: Enhance SymbolicExprContext and SymbolicMap Equality
body:
Enhance SymbolicExprContext and SymbolicMap Equality

We are introducing an operator== for SymbolicExprContext to allow comparison based on the underlying mlir::MLIRContext pointer and updating the SymbolicMap::operator== has been updated to use this new SymbolicExprContext::operator==. 

This change ensures that two SymbolicMap instances are considered equal if they have the same number of dimensions, symbols, and expressions, even if they are associated with different SymbolicExprContext objects, as long as those contexts point to the same mlir::MLIRContext. This is crucial because SymbolicExpr instances are uniqued within a specific StorageUniquer, so expressions from contexts sharing the same MLIRContext are inherently equivalent. This is needed to make IndexingMapTest::IndexingMapSupportsAbslHashAndEqAndNe to pass with SymbolicMaps.
